- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 30d horizon.
- If official event net supply is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates true drop; add 3–8% downward adjustment.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is rising steadily from low base, true outcome often pulls back; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7d high.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and event supply is high, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–15% for 30d horizon.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and net supply < -10, apply “event-driven correction”: subtract 1.5–3.0% from forecast for each additional event beyond 15.
